title: collections: Counter, deque
short: Counter, defaultdict and deque save you lines and bugs.
what: The collections module has three tools interviews use all the time. Counter counts things. defaultdict fills in a starting value for a missing key. deque is a list that is fast at both ends, the right type for a queue.
analogy: A tally sheet that adds a new row by itself the first time a name shows up, and a ticket line where people can join or leave at either end.

frames.label: Counter("banana")
frames.say: Counter("banana") counts the letters for you in one pass. Here it has read b, a, n: each new letter starts at 1.

frames.label: Counter("banana")
frames.say: The rest, "ana", bumps a to 3 and n to 2. No get(), no KeyError: a missing letter reads as 0.

frames.label: c.most_common(2)
frames.say: most_common(2) returns the 2 biggest counts, largest first. That is the "top k frequent" step in one call.

frames.label: groups = defaultdict(list)
frames.say: defaultdict(list) makes an empty list the first time you touch a key. groups[len(w)].append(w) needs no check.

frames.label: groups[len(w)].append(w)
frames.say: "ox" makes a new key 2; "dog" finds key 3 and joins "cat". Words are now grouped by length.

frames.label: print(groups[9])
frames.say: Careful: even reading groups[9] creates the key with []. Use 9 in groups to check without adding.

frames.label: deg = defaultdict(int)
frames.say: defaultdict(int) starts every new key at 0, so deg["a"] += 1 works with no check. Handy for counting in-degrees.

frames.label: q = deque([1, 2, 3])
frames.say: deque is fast at both ends: append and pop work on the right, appendleft and popleft on the left. All O(1).

when: Count how often each item appears
Group items into lists by a key
Add or remove at both ends
python:
from collections import Counter, defaultdict, deque
c = Counter("banana")
print(c, c["z"], c.most_common(2))
groups = defaultdict(list)
for w in ["cat", "ox", "dog"]:
    groups[len(w)].append(w)
print(dict(groups), 9 in groups)
deg = defaultdict(int)
deg["a"] += 1
print(dict(deg))
q = deque([1, 2, 3])
q.append(4)
q.appendleft(0)
print(q.popleft(), q.pop(), q)
watch: Reading a missing key in a defaultdict creates it. Check with key in d first.
A BFS queue should be a deque with popleft(). list.pop(0) is O(n) each time.
Counter subtraction (c1 - c2) drops every count that falls to 0 or below.
